question: Which of the following Indian languages is NOT categorised as a classical language by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __Bengali.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bengali is not categorised as a classical language by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.**
 
• Bengali:
 
 
• It also known as Bangla.
 
• It is an Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly in the Indian state of West Bengal and the sovereign country of Bangladesh.
 
• It holds the status of one of the 22 scheduled languages of India.
 
• Bengali literature has a rich heritage, with contributions from renowned poets, novelists, and playwrights. Notable figures include Rabindranath Tagore, the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature, and Kazi Nazrul Islam, known as the "Rebel Poet."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​In the Rajya Sabha, the Ministry of Culture specified the requirements for designating a language as "Classical":

 
 
• Uniqueness: The literature and languages of the ancient era should be distinguished from their modern equivalents.
 
• Individuality: The literary heritage ought to be original and shouldn't be taken from another language group.
 
• Magnificent Legacy: It ought to have a collection of antique books and manuscripts that have been treasured for ages.
 
• High Antiquity: The language needs to have a 1500–2000 years historical record.
 
 
 
• There are six classical languages in India currently. They are:
 
 
• Tamil.
 
• Sanskrit.
 
• Kannada.
 
• Telugu.
 
• Malayalam.
 
• Odia.
